solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Like Lincoln, perhaps, quiet and designed for living in

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
residential describes buildings or areas meant for homes

explanation.surface: A description of a quiet house built purely as a home, with a nod to Abraham Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like Lincoln' suggests the log cabin he grew up in, but the definition looks to his office.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham Lincoln held the office of US president, so something like him, perhaps, belongs to that office.

clue.text: Unwilling chap entered in further exam

indicators.note: the chap's name is entered into the middle of the exam word

parts.note: a resit is an exam taken again after failing
Stan is a man's name, standing for any chap

explanation.surface: A man reluctant to sit another exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone resistant to an idea opposes it, so is unwilling to go along with it.

clue.text: Importance of land surrounding ancient city

indicators.note: the land word wraps around the city word

parts.note: a state is a country or land
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: The significance of a country that encircles a city from antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature means standing or reputation, a synonym for importance or eminence.

clue.text: Tramp, maybe — one omitted from file

indicators.note: the letter for one is left out of the file word

parts.note: a dossier is a file of documents on a subject
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A vagrant's details missing from an official file.
explanation.walkthrough: A dosser is British slang for a homeless person who sleeps rough, or an idler.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is one example of a dosser, someone who beds down rough, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Operatic heroine, and not mother!

parts.note: nor means and not, as in neither this nor that
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: An opera's leading lady who turns out to be childless.
explanation.walkthrough: Norma is the title heroine of Bellini's opera, a Druid priestess who is in fact a mother, which the exclamation teases.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellini's opera is named after its tragic Druid priestess protagonist, an operatic heroine.

clue.text: Anger when leader is removed from republic

indicators.note: the first letter of the republic's name is taken away; the letters running backwards across these words are a coincidence

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland

explanation.surface: Fury erupts when a head of state is deposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary synonym for wrath or fury.

clue.text: Like the squire touching down outside old quarters

indicators.note: the touching down word sits outside the other letters

parts.note: landing is what an aircraft does when touching down
W and N, west and north, are two of the compass quarters

explanation.surface: A country squire's plane landing beyond some old lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' reads as lodgings but gives two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A squire was traditionally the chief owner of land in an English village, so he is property-holding.

clue.text: A Welsh girl abandoning centre of Conwy for continent

indicators.note: the girl's name gives up the letter that follows

parts.note: Sian is a Welsh girl's name

indicators.note: the middle letter of Conwy is chosen

explanation.surface: A Welsh woman leaving the middle of Conwy, a town in North Wales, to go abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest of the continents on Earth.

clue.text: Male offspring entertaining whim to become medic

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold within, so the offspring word holds the whim word

parts.note: a son is a male child
an urge is a sudden impulse or whim

explanation.surface: A son taking a fancy to train as a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a doctor who operates, one kind of medic.

clue.text: Widely divergent, like citizens of Warsaw and Cracow?

definitions.meaning: the idiom for being completely different in views

definitions.text: like citizens of Warsaw and Cracow?
definitions.meaning: residents of two Polish cities are Polish people living a long way from each other

explanation.surface: Two cities' inhabitants who see things very differently.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at opposite extremes, as the North and South geographic ends are; literally, Polish people separated by distance.

clue.text: Inconspicuous former pupil's remedy

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school, plus the S of the possessive
a cure is a remedy for illness

explanation.surface: An unremarkable cure belonging to an old boy of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure is little known or hard to notice, so unnoticeable.

clue.text: A posh girl originally organising sound reproduction

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U usage
Di, short for Diana, is a girl's name

indicators.note: the first letter of organising is taken

explanation.surface: An upper-class young woman setting up a stereo system.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio refers to recorded or transmitted sound, as in audio equipment.

clue.text: Society girl Italian poet takes in underground going north

indicators.note: the poet's name takes the other letters into itself

parts.note: Dante Alighieri wrote the Divine Comedy

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Tube is the London Underground

explanation.surface: A young socialite and a famous Italian riding the London metro northward.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young upper-class woman making her first appearance in fashionable society.

clue.text: Over the moon, no longer living in outskirts of Enfield

indicators.note: the deceased word goes inside the outer letters
the outer letters of Enfield, its first and last

parts.note: late means deceased, as in the late king

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled, though dead, at the edge of Enfield, a north London suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the moon is an idiom for being extremely happy and delighted.

clue.text: Primate backing big toff from the east?

indicators.note: backing means the words run in reverse order
reading from the east in an across clue means right to left

parts.note: a nob is a posh person, a toff

explanation.surface: An ape supporting a large posh gentleman from eastern parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibbon is a small long-armed ape, one of the primates.

clue.text: Cut off one's oxygen behind time

parts.note: I for one, plus the S of one's
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
late means behind schedule

explanation.surface: Someone's air supply is severed after running out of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to separate or set apart from others, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Burn printed music mostly used by church

indicators.note: most of the music word is kept, dropping its final letter

parts.note: a score is the written or printed form of a musical work

explanation.surface: Sheet music used by a church gets set on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch is to singe a surface, a light burn.

clue.text: A longing to be head of Harrow, perhaps?

definitions.note: the first letter of the word Harrow, an example of the letter H

parts.note: an itch is a strong desire or longing

explanation.surface: Wanting to become headmaster of Harrow, a famous English public school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of Harrow' suggests a headmaster; it means the first letter of the word Harrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The spelt-out name of the letter H, which begins Harrow, is the head of that word.

clue.text: Hoofed mammal — or husky, do we hear?

indicators.note: this asks whether the word sounds the same when spoken

parts.note: a husky voice is hoarse

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a sled dog counts as a hoofed animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husky' suggests the sled dog, an animal to match the surface, but it means a rough voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse is an ungulate, a mammal with hooves.

clue.text: Piece of toasted bread criminal eats right away

indicators.note: the criminal word swallows the other letters

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
out means away, as in out of the office

explanation.surface: A crook wolfing down a bit of toast immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' reads as at once but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a small cube of fried or toasted bread served in soup or salad.

clue.text: One who hopes to have a run round part of church

indicators.note: the a and run letters go round the church part

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a spire is the tall pointed top of a church tower

explanation.surface: A hopeful person jogging around a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirer is someone with ambitions, who aims or hopes to achieve something.

clue.text: State of equality father respected at first

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: the first letter of respected is taken

explanation.surface: A father respected as an equal from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a par means being level with, so the word names equal standing.

clue.text: River featuring in popular novel

indicators.note: the letters feature inside the words popular novel

explanation.surface: A river that appears in a best-selling book.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arno is the Italian river that flows through Florence and Pisa.

clue.text: Here we let her put out a light vehicle

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Telling someone to let a woman out of a small car.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-wheeler is a small lightweight car or tricycle with three wheels.
